title: How the instructor built a swimmer
body:
Read the extract and answer the question that follows.

"Then he taught me to put my face under water and exhale, and to raise my nose and inhale. I repeated the exercise hundreds of times. Bit by bit I shed part of the panic that seized me when my head went under water. Next he held me at the side of the pool and had me kick with my legs. For weeks I did just that. At first my legs refused to work. But they gradually relaxed; and finally I could command them. Thus, piece by piece, he built a swimmer. And when he had perfected each piece, he put them together into an integrated whole. In April he said, 'Now you can swim. Dive off and swim the length of the pool, crawl stroke.' I did. The instructor was finished. But I was not finished."

(From 'Deep Water' by William O. Douglas, NCERT Flamingo, Class 12)
